0.title: Lesson 1: How VR Headsets Work
From Flat Screens to 360° Headsets
0.desc: When you watch TV or play on a computer, you look at a flat screen in front of you. But in case of a VR headset, it is worn over your eyes so the screen surrounds your entire view. Wherever you turn your head—up, down, left, or right then you experience a full 360° digital world!
0.funFact: The very first virtual reality machine was built in 1962! Called the 'Sensorama', it let viewers ride a virtual motorcycle with 3D visuals, stereo sound, wind, and even flower scents!

1.title: How Two Eyes See 3D Depth
1.desc: Try closing one eye, then the other—notice how your left and right eyes see from slightly different angles? VR headsets use this same natural trick! Inside the headset, two separate images are shown (one for each eye). Your brain combines them to see realistic 3D depth and distance.
1.funFact: Because our two eyes are slightly apart, each sees a slightly different angle. VR headsets use this principle called stereoscopy to create true 3D depth inside flat displays!

2.title: 3D Sound That Moves With You
2.desc: VR doesn't just trick your eyes.It uses 3D Spatial Audio for your ears. If a virtual rocket takes off to your right, the sound comes from the right earphone. When you turn your head toward the rocket, the sound moves right in front of you.
2.funFact: NASA astronauts train for real spacewalks inside VR headsets before ever leaving Earth, practicing how to use tools in zero gravity!

0.summary: Discover how VR headsets surround your eyes with 360-degree digital worlds!

1.title: Lesson 2: Lenses & Motion Sensors

0.title: Why VR Headsets Need Lenses
0.desc: If you hold a phone screen two inches from your nose, it looks blurry and hurts your eyes. VR headsets place special curved glass lenses between your eyes and the screen. These lenses bend light rays so your eyes can focus clearly without straining.
0.funFact: VR headset lenses use concentric Fresnel grooves to stay extremely thin and light while bending display light precisely to your eyes!

1.title: Gyroscope Motion Sensors
1.desc:
How does the virtual world move instantly when you turn your head?
 • Inside the headset is a tiny sensor called a Gyroscope. It measures your head turns more than 1,000 times every second so the camera moves exactly when you move!
1.funFact: A modern VR gyroscope measures head turns over 1,000 times per second—more than 10 times faster than the blink of a human eye!

2.title: Fast Screen Refresh Rate
2.desc: If a screen updates too slowly when you look around, it can make you feel dizzy. Good VR headsets refresh the picture 90 to 120 times every single second! This super-fast speed keeps motion smooth and natural.
2.funFact: Human eyes notice motion lag if it takes more than 20 milliseconds. Modern VR screens refresh up to 120 times every second!

1.summary: Learn how curved glass lenses keep screens clear and how smart sensors track your head.

2.title: Lesson 3: Controllers & Touch Feedback

0.title: Tracking Your Hands in 3D Space
0.desc: To grab objects in VR, you hold wireless hand controllers. Cameras on the headset track hidden infrared lights on the controllers. When you raise your real hand or wave, your virtual hand inside the headset moves the exact same way!
0.funFact: VR controllers have tiny hidden infrared LEDs that cameras track with sub-millimeter precision in 3D space!

1.title: Buttons, Joysticks & Grab Triggers
1.desc: VR controllers have joysticks for walking and trigger buttons under your fingers. When you squeeze the trigger button, your virtual hand closes to pick up lab beakers, throw a basketball, or use scientific tools.
1.funFact: Advanced VR gloves can simulate physical resistance so grabbing a virtual baseball or bow feels solid and real in your hand!

2.title: Feeling Virtual Contact (Haptic Vibration)
2.desc:
Have you noticed how a phone vibrates when you get a notification? 
• VR controllers use tiny vibration motors inside. When your virtual hand touches a table or catches a ball, the controller rumbles so you actually feel the contact!
2.funFact: Haptic feedback uses linear resonant actuators. The exact same ultra-precise vibration motors used in high-end smartphones!

2.summary: Find out how wireless controllers track your hands and vibrate when you touch virtual objects!

3.title: Lesson 4: VR vs. AR vs. Mixed Reality
3.titleShort: VR vs. AR vs. Mixed Reality

0.title: Virtual Reality (VR) - Full Digital World
0.desc: In Virtual Reality (VR), your view of the real room is completely replaced by a computer-generated 3D world. You can visit outer space, dive deep into the ocean, or walk inside an atom simulation.
0.funFact: Surgeons practice complex brain and heart operations inside VR medical simulators before ever operating on a real patient!

1.title: Augmented Reality (AR) - Digital Overlays
1.desc: Augmented Reality (AR) lets you see your real physical room while adding digital information or pictures on top. For example, pointing a tablet camera at a plant to see floating labels of its leaves and roots.
1.funFact: Pilots have used head-up augmented reality displays projected onto jet cockpits since the late 1970s!

2.title: Mixed Reality (MR) - Interaction
2.desc: Mixed Reality (MR) is the newest technology. It mixes the real and virtual worlds so they interact. You could have a virtual pet dog that actually hides behind your real physical sofa!
2.funFact: Advanced MR headsets scan your actual room in real-time, mapping every wall, chair, and table so digital objects can bounce off them.

3.summary: Understand the difference between full virtual worlds and digital holograms in your room!

4.title: Lesson 5: Safety & Eye Care in VR

0.title: Taking Breaks to Prevent Eye Strain
0.desc: Staring at any screen for too long can tire your eyes. In VR, it's important to follow the 20-20-20 rule. Every 20 minutes, take off the headset and look at something at least 20 feet away for 20 seconds to relax your eye muscles.
0.funFact: Your blink rate drops by half when staring at a screen, which causes dry eyes. Remembering to blink often helps keep your eyes comfortable!

1.title: Clearing Your Real-World Play Space
1.desc: When you are in VR, you cannot see your real room. Always clear your play space of toys, chairs, or pets before putting on the headset. Setting up a 'Guardian Boundary' helps warn you if you get too close to a wall.
1.funFact: Some modern headsets have a 'pass-through' feature that instantly turns on the outside cameras if you step out of your safe zone!

2.title: Listening to Your Body
2.desc: If you ever feel dizzy, tired, or motion sick while playing VR, immediately take the headset off and take a break. Your brain needs time to adjust to moving in a virtual world while your physical body stands still.
2.funFact: Motion sickness in VR happens because your eyes tell your brain you are moving, but your inner ear balance system says you are standing still!

4.summary: Discover the golden rules for using VR safely without straining your eyes.

heritage.heroDesc: Discover, learn and preserve our rich history and cultural heritage in a new interactive way.
heritage.fc_TheIndusValley_desc: Discover the advanced urban planning of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. They featured baked brick houses, elaborate drainage systems, and water supply systems.
heritage.fc_TheIndusValley_full:
The Indus Valley Civilization was one of the earliest urban societies in human history, flourishing across northwestern South Asia. Renowned for their planned cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, the citizens built standardized baked brick houses arranged in orderly grid patterns.

What makes this civilization remarkable is its emphasis on public health and civic engineering. Every dwelling was connected to a sophisticated underground drainage and sewage network that surpassed any other ancient society. They engaged in widespread sea and land trade, utilizing uniform stone weights and seals engraved with animals and an undeciphered script.
heritage.fc_Mesopotamia_desc: Known as the cradle of civilization, located between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, famous for the invention of writing.
heritage.fc_Mesopotamia_full:
Mesopotamia, located between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, is widely regarded as the cradle of civilization. It was here that humanity established its first organized cities, formal legal codes, and agricultural surpluses supported by extensive irrigation.

Around 3200 BCE, Mesopotamian scribes invented cuneiform, the first written script, pressed into soft clay tablets. The society also pioneered wheel-making for transport and pottery, advanced astronomy, and monumental architecture exemplified by towering stepped temples known as ziggurats.
heritage.fc_AncientEgypt_desc: Explore the civilization of the Nile Valley, known for its monumental pyramids, pharaohs, and hieroglyphic writing system.
heritage.fc_AncientEgypt_full:
Ancient Egypt developed along the fertile banks of the Nile River, creating a stable kingdom ruled by monarchs known as pharaohs. The annual flood of the Nile provided rich soil that allowed Egyptian agriculture and culture to thrive over three millennia.

Egyptian engineers constructed enduring monuments, including the limestone Pyramids of Giza and grand temple complexes. They developed hieroglyphic script, advanced medical practices, geometry for land surveying, and papyrus sheets that served as early writing paper.
heritage.fc_AncientRome_desc: A massive empire that shaped Western civilization, known for its engineering, architecture, and complex legal and political systems.
heritage.fc_AncientRome_full:
Originating as a republic along the Tiber River, Rome expanded into a vast empire encompassing the entire Mediterranean basin. Roman jurisprudence laid foundational principles for modern legal and governmental frameworks across the world.

Roman civil engineering transformed civic life through enduring infrastructure. By developing strong volcanic concrete, they constructed thousands of miles of paved roads, monumental public baths, stone aqueducts to transport fresh water, and amphitheaters such as the Colosseum.
heritage.fc_MayanCivilization_desc: A Mesoamerican civilization noted for its fully developed writing system, art, architecture, mathematics, and astronomical system.
heritage.fc_MayanCivilization_full:
The Maya civilization flourished across tropical Mesoamerica, building independent city-states connected by trade networks. They are distinguished by their sophisticated hieroglyphic writing system capable of recording historical events and astronomical cycles.

Mayan mathematicians independently conceived the concept of zero, allowing them to perform complex calculations and develop highly precise solar calendars. Their architects constructed stepped stone pyramids, observatories, and palaces amidst dense tropical forests.
heritage.fc_TheCholaDynasty_desc: Learn about the powerful Chola empire, their art, and architecture. They were known for building grand temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple.
heritage.fc_TheCholaDynasty_full:
The Chola Dynasty was one of the longest-ruling empires in Indian history, celebrated for their administrative efficiency, maritime commerce, and Dravidian temple architecture. Their naval expeditions established trade routes stretching across Southeast Asia.

Under rulers like Rajaraja Chola I, they constructed grand granite temples such as the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur. Chola artisans also perfected the lost-wax casting technique to produce exquisite bronze sculptures, most notably the cosmic representation of Shiva as Nataraja.
heritage.fc_TajMahal_desc: An immense mausoleum of white marble, built in Agra by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his favorite wife.
heritage.fc_TajMahal_full:
Commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, the Taj Mahal stands as an iconic achievement of Indo-Islamic architecture. Located along the banks of the Yamuna River, the complex integrates Persian, Islamic, and Indian design principles.

The white marble structure is renowned for its symmetrical balance, reflecting pools, and intricate pietra dura stonework. Artisans inlaid semi-precious stones directly into the marble walls to depict delicate floral motifs and calligraphy.
heritage.fc_AjantaEllora_desc: Ancient rock-cut caves featuring magnificent Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain sculptures and paintings dating back to the 2nd century BCE.
heritage.fc_AjantaEllora_full:
The Ajanta and Ellora Caves represent the pinnacle of Indian rock-cut architecture. Over centuries, master artisans carved detailed monasteries, prayer halls, and monumental sculptures directly into basalt cliffs.

Ajanta is celebrated for its ancient Buddhist mural paintings depicting Jataka tales with natural mineral pigments. Ellora features sanctuaries representing Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism side by side, including the Kailasa Temple, which was excavated top-down from a single solid rock.
heritage.fc_VijayanagaraEmpire_desc: The ruins of Hampi tell the story of a prosperous and wealthy empire known for its intricate temple architecture and grand bazaars.
heritage.fc_VijayanagaraEmpire_full:
The Vijayanagara Empire served as a prominent cultural and economic power in South India. Its capital at Hampi was described by contemporary international travelers as one of the wealthiest and largest trading cities of its era.

The surviving ruins showcase distinct Dravidian stone architecture, featuring ornate pillared halls, aqueducts, royal pavilions, and the iconic Stone Chariot at the Vittala Temple complex.
heritage.fc_KhajurahoTemples_desc: Famous for their nagara-style architectural symbolism and intricate, expressive sculptures built by the Chandela dynasty.
heritage.fc_KhajurahoTemples_full:
Constructed by the Chandela dynasty between 950 and 1050 CE, the Khajuraho Group of Monuments represents classic Nagara-style North Indian temple architecture. Out of 85 original temples dedicated to Hindu and Jain deities, around 25 remain well preserved today.

The temples are constructed from sandstone without mortar, relying on precise mortise-and-tenon interlocking joints. Their outer walls are adorned with thousands of finely carved sculptures depicting artistic celebrations, music, dance, and everyday community life.
heritage.fc_TheGreatWall_desc: Explore the history and construction of the majestic Great Wall of China, built to protect against nomadic intrusions.
heritage.fc_TheGreatWall_full:
The Great Wall of China is an extensive series of stone and earth fortifications extending across northern China. Built over successive dynasties over two millennia, its primary function was defensive protection along the northern frontier.

Beyond military defense, the fortifications facilitated border control, regulated trade along the Silk Road, and served as an integrated communication corridor utilizing watchtowers and signal stations.
heritage.fc_MachuPicchu_desc: An Incan citadel set high in the Andes Mountains in Peru, renowned for its sophisticated dry-stone walls and panoramic views.
heritage.fc_MachuPicchu_full:
Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel situated on a mountain ridge nearly 8,000 feet above sea level in the Peruvian Andes. Built during the reign of Emperor Pachacuti, it served as an imperial estate and religious sanctuary.

The site demonstrates advanced Inca engineering adapted to mountainous terrain. It features polished dry-stone masonry fitted without mortar, extensive agricultural terracing to prevent soil erosion, and stone aqueducts providing fresh spring water.
heritage.fc_Colosseum_desc: An oval amphitheater in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy, built of travertine limestone, tuff, and brick-faced concrete.
heritage.fc_Colosseum_full:
The Colosseum, originally named the Flavian Amphitheater, is the largest standing amphitheater in the world. Constructed of travertine limestone and Roman concrete, it could seat up to 50,000 spectators for civic assemblies and public performances.

The monument demonstrates sophisticated structural design, utilizing tiered arches and vaulting. Below the wooden arena floor lay the hypogeum, a complex network of underground tunnels and mechanical elevators used to transport stage scenery.
heritage.fc_RosettaStone_desc: A granodiorite stele inscribed with three versions of a decree that became the key to deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphs.
heritage.fc_RosettaStone_full:
The Rosetta Stone is an ancient Egyptian granodiorite stele inscribed with a royal decree issued at Memphis on behalf of King Ptolemy V. The inscription appears in three distinct scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphic, Demotic script, and Ancient Greek.

Because scholars could read the Greek text, the Rosetta Stone provided the linguistic key necessary to decipher ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics in 1822, opening thousands of years of recorded Egyptian history to modern study.
heritage.fc_DancingGirl_desc: A prehistoric bronze sculpture made in lost-wax casting, found in Mohenjo-daro, a symbol of the Indus Valley civilization.
heritage.fc_DancingGirl_full:
The Dancing Girl is a prehistoric bronze statuette discovered in 1926 among the archaeological ruins of Mohenjo-daro. Standing approximately 10.5 centimeters tall, it represents one of the earliest examples of metal sculpture in South Asia.

Created using the lost-wax metallurgical casting process, the figurine depicts a young woman standing in a confident posture adorned with traditional arm bangles, illustrating the metallurgical skill and artistic expression of Indus Valley society.
heritage.fc_VenusdeMilo_desc: An ancient Greek marble sculpture, one of the most famous works of ancient Greek sculpture, depicting Aphrodite.
heritage.fc_VenusdeMilo_full:
The Venus de Milo is an ancient Greek marble sculpture created during the Hellenistic period, attributed to Alexandros of Antioch. Discovered on the Aegean island of Milos in 1820, it depicts Aphrodite, the Greek goddess of beauty.

Standing over two meters tall, the sculpture is admired for the naturalistic rendering of drapery wrapping around the lower body and classic proportioning, serving as a landmark example of classical Hellenistic artistic mastery.
heritage.fc_VedicScripts_desc: Understand the ancient wisdom preserved in the oldest Sanskrit texts, encompassing philosophy, rituals, and hymns.
heritage.fc_VedicScripts_full:
The Vedas are the foundational scriptures of ancient Indian literature and philosophical thought. Composed in classical Vedic Sanskrit, they represent some of the oldest preserved body of literature in human civilization.

Consisting of four primary collections—the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda—the texts were preserved for centuries through rigorous oral transmission before being recorded in manuscript form. They contain philosophical treatises, ethical principles, and hymns celebrating nature.
heritage.fc_DeadSeaScrolls_desc: Ancient Jewish religious manuscripts found in the Qumran Caves in the Judaean Desert, of great historical and religious significance.
heritage.fc_DeadSeaScrolls_full:
The Dead Sea Scrolls comprise over 900 ancient religious manuscripts discovered inside earthenware jars across the Qumran Caves near the Dead Sea between 1947 and 1956.

Written on parchment, papyrus, and copper in Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek, the collection contains the oldest known surviving manuscripts of biblical books along with historical records of community life during the Second Temple period.
heritage.fc_MagnaCarta_desc: A royal charter of rights agreed to by King John of England, laying the foundation for modern democracy and constitutional law.
heritage.fc_MagnaCarta_full:
The Magna Carta (Great Charter) was issued by King John of England at Runnymede in June 1215. Written on parchment in medieval Latin, it established the principle that everyone, including the sovereign ruler, is subject to the rule of law.

The document guaranteed due process of law and protection against arbitrary taxation and illegal imprisonment, serving as a foundational influence on modern constitutional democracies and international civil rights.
heritage.fc_BookofKells_desc: An illuminated manuscript Gospel book in Latin, containing the four Gospels of the New Testament, renowned for its intricate artwork.
heritage.fc_BookofKells_full:
The Book of Kells is a masterwork of medieval illuminated manuscript art created by Celtic monks around 800 CE. Preserved at Trinity College Dublin, it contains the four Gospels of the Christian New Testament written in Latin.

The calfskin vellum pages are decorated with intricate interlace patterns, Celtic knotwork, and vivid mineral pigments imported across continent-spanning trade routes.
heritage.fc_GutenbergBible_desc: The first major book printed using mass-produced movable metal type in Europe, marking the start of the printing revolution.
heritage.fc_GutenbergBible_full:
Completed around 1455 by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz, Germany, the Gutenberg Bible was the first major publication produced in Europe using movable metal type and a mechanical printing press.

This technological advancement replaced labor-intensive manual manuscript copying, significantly reducing the cost of books and enabling the widespread dissemination of scientific, philosophical, and literary knowledge across Europe.
heritage.fc_Revoltof1857_desc: Also known as the First War of Independence, it was a major uprising in India against the rule of the British East India Company.
heritage.fc_Revoltof1857_full:
The Revolt of 1857 marked the first widespread resistance against the administration of the British East India Company. Involving soldiers, regional rulers, peasants, and civil leaders across northern and central India, it united diverse communities in defiance of colonial rule.

Prominent figures including Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, Veer Kunwar Singh of Bihar, and Tatya Tope led defense movements that directly inspired subsequent generations of Indian national leadership.
heritage.fc_JallianwalaBagh_desc: A turning point in the Indian independence movement where peaceful protestors were fired upon by British colonial troops.
heritage.fc_JallianwalaBagh_full:
On April 13, 1919, thousands of unarmed citizens gathered peacefully at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar on the occasion of Baisakhi. British colonial troops blocked the main exit and fired upon the assembly.

The event served as a definitive turning point in the Indian independence movement, fostering nationwide unity and reinforcing national determination for self-governance.
heritage.fc_PartitionofIndia_desc: The division of British India into two independent dominions, India and Pakistan, marking the end of colonial rule.
heritage.fc_PartitionofIndia_full:
In August 1947, British colonial rule concluded with the independence and partition of the Indian subcontinent into two independent sovereign nations: India and Pakistan.

Following independence, India established a parliamentary democratic constitution guaranteeing equal civic rights, institutional representation, and secular governance across its diverse populations.
heritage.fc_MadhubaniArt_desc: Learn the vibrant storytelling traditions of Bihar through mural paintings, traditionally created by women in the Mithila region.
heritage.fc_MadhubaniArt_full:
Madhubani painting, also known as Mithila art, originated in the Mithila region of Bihar. Traditionally painted by women on freshly plastered mud walls during festivals and weddings, the art form represents historical narratives and natural symbolism.

Artisans utilize natural plant-derived pigments extracted from turmeric, marigold flowers, indigo, and soot. Characterized by intricate geometric border designs and vibrant imagery, no space on the surface is left unadorned.
heritage.fc_WarliPainting_desc: A tribal art form from Maharashtra that uses geometric shapes to depict social life, deeply rooted in nature and community.
heritage.fc_WarliPainting_full:
Warli painting is a traditional indigenous art form created by tribal communities in Maharashtra. Unlike religious iconography, Warli art portrays everyday social life, community farming, and natural ecosystems.

Executed predominantly in white pigment made from rice paste mixed with water and tree gum on earth-toned clay walls, the artists use geometric shapes—circles representing the sun and moon, and triangles representing human figures and mountains.
heritage.fc_KalbeliaDance_desc: A sensuous folk dance performed by the women of the Kalbelia snake-charming community in Rajasthan, India.
heritage.fc_KalbeliaDance_full:
Kalbelia is a traditional folk dance performed by the Kalbelia community of Rajasthan. Recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, the dance mirrors the graceful movements of desert serpents.

Female performers wear flowing embroidered black skirts adorned with silver mirror-work, dancing to traditional percussion instruments and the woodwind pungi.
heritage.fc_KathputliPuppetry_desc: A string puppet theatre native to Rajasthan, known for its vibrant storytelling, colorful dolls, and traditional music.
heritage.fc_KathputliPuppetry_full:
Kathputli is a traditional string puppet theater native to Rajasthan. The name derives from "Kath" meaning wood and "Putli" meaning doll. The tradition has been passed down through generations of folk performers.

Carved from mango wood and painted with expressive features, the puppets are manipulated with fine strings by puppeteers who narrate historical legends, moral lessons, and regional folklore.
heritage.fc_BaulSingers_desc: Mystic minstrels from Bengal whose music blends various religious influences, emphasizing a search for the inner divine.
heritage.fc_BaulSingers_full:
The Bauls are a community of mystic minstrels from Bengal known for their oral musical tradition celebrating universal humanity and inner spiritual harmony.

Performing with traditional acoustic instruments such as the one-stringed ektara and hand drums, Baul poetry emphasizes kindness, tolerance, and brotherhood beyond social boundaries.
heritage.fc_Petra_desc: A famous archaeological site in Jordan's southwestern desert, known for its rock-cut architecture and water conduit system.
heritage.fc_Petra_full:
Petra served as the flourishing capital of the Nabataean Kingdom, strategically positioned at the crossroads of ancient Arabian spice and incense trade routes. The city is famous for its rose-toned sandstone facades carved directly into desert canyons.

To thrive in an arid desert environment, Nabataean engineers constructed an elaborate water management system composed of terracotta pipelines, dams, and rock-cut cisterns that stored seasonal flash floods for year-round supply.
heritage.fc_ChichenItza_desc: A complex of Mayan ruins on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, dominated by the massive El Castillo step pyramid.
heritage.fc_ChichenItza_full:
Chichen Itza was a major urban and ceremonial center of the Maya-Toltec civilization on the Yucatán Peninsula. The site reflects a synthesis of Mayan architectural traditions and Central Mexican design influences.

At its center stands El Castillo (the Temple of Kukulcan), a stepped pyramid aligned precisely with solar equinoxes. The pyramid features 365 steps corresponding to the solar year, demonstrating the builders' accurate astronomical knowledge.
heritage.fc_TerracottaWarriors_desc: Uncover the secrets of the massive underground army of the first Emperor of China, buried with him to protect him in the afterlife.
heritage.fc_TerracottaWarriors_full:
The Terracotta Army is a collection of thousands of life-sized terracotta sculptures depicting the armies of Qin Shi Huang, the first Emperor of China. Buried near his imperial mausoleum, the figures were intended to guard the monarch in the afterlife.

Discovered in 1974, the collection includes over 8,000 soldiers, chariots, and cavalry horses. Each sculpture was crafted with distinct facial features, hairstyles, and armor, representing the administrative and artistic capability of ancient China.
heritage.fc_TutankhamunsMask_desc: The gold death mask of the 18th-dynasty ancient Egyptian Pharaoh Tutankhamun, discovered by Howard Carter in 1925.
heritage.fc_TutankhamunsMask_full:
The funerary mask of Tutankhamun is one of the most recognized artworks of Ancient Egypt. Discovered intact in 1925 inside his tomb in the Valley of the Kings, it rested directly over the mummified remains of the young pharaoh.

Crafted from high-purity solid gold weighing over 10 kilograms, the mask is inlaid with colored glass, quartz, obsidian, and lapis lazuli. The royal headdress features the royal insignia of the vulture and cobra, symbolizing sovereignty over Upper and Lower Egypt.
heritage.fc_TheSaltMarch_desc: Trace the path of non-violent resistance that changed the world, led by Mahatma Gandhi against the British salt monopoly.
heritage.fc_TheSaltMarch_loc: Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, Gujarat, India
heritage.fc_TheSaltMarch_full:
The Salt March (Dandi Satyagraha) was a landmark non-violent civil disobedience movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930 against colonial taxation and the British salt monopoly.

Over 24 days, Gandhi and thousands of citizens marched 240 miles on foot from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi, where they harvested natural salt from seawater. The protest drew global attention to India's independence movement and demonstrated the efficacy of peaceful non-cooperation.
heritage.fc_QuitIndiaMovement_desc: Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942, demanding an end to British rule in India during World War II.
heritage.fc_QuitIndiaMovement_full:
Launched on August 8, 1942, at the Bombay session of the All-India Congress Committee, the Quit India Movement demanded an immediate end to colonial rule across India.

Following Mahatma Gandhi's call to action, students, workers, and rural populations engaged in nationwide demonstrations, strikes, and underground information networks that significantly accelerated India's transition toward complete independence.

cyber.content_MASTERINGCYBERSECURI_0eae:
MASTERING CYBER SECURITY TERMINOLOGY

• Phishing: Deceptive communications disguised as legitimate entities designed to trick users into disclosing sensitive credentials.
• Ransomware: Malicious software that encrypts user files and demands financial ransom for the decryption key.
• Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): A security mechanism requiring two or more independent credentials to verify user identity.
• Zero-Day Exploit: A cyber attack targeting a newly discovered software vulnerability before a patch is available.
• End-to-End Encryption: Cryptographic protocols that secure data in transit so only authorized recipients can decipher it.
• Social Engineering: Psychological manipulation techniques used by threat actors to breach human security barriers.
cyber.content_PROTECTINGYOURONLINE_b167:
PROTECTING YOUR ONLINE IDENTIFIER & FOOTPRINT

1. Practice Data Minimization: Never enter unnecessary personal details on public web forms.
2. Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) on all financial and primary email accounts.
3. Audit Application Permissions: Regularly revoke microphone, location, and background data access from unused apps.
4. Use Unique Passwords: Avoid credential reuse across multiple web platforms.
5. Inspect URLs Carefully: Verify HTTPS protocol and exact domain spelling before entering authentication credentials.
6. Keep Software Updated: System updates contain critical patches for known exploits.
7. Avoid Unsecured Public Wi-Fi: Use a trusted VPN or mobile network when logging into private accounts on public networks.
8. Restrict Social & Profile Privacy: Regularly audit privacy settings to ensure only trusted contacts view your posts and personal details.
9. Protect OTPs & Verification Codes: Never share One-Time Passwords with anyone—banks and platform admins will never request them.
10. Think Before You Post: Remember that everything shared online leaves a lasting digital footprint—be mindful of location tags, personal photos, and sensitive data.
cyber.content_IMMEDIATERESPONSEPRO_bb99:
IMMEDIATE RESPONSE PROTOCOL FOR COMPROMISED ACCOUNTS

Step 1: Isolate the Affected Device — Disconnect from Wi-Fi or cellular networks to prevent lateral malware spread.
Step 2: Reset Primary Credentials — Use a clean, uncompromised device to reset passwords for your primary email and bank accounts.
Step 3: Terminate Active Sessions — Use account security settings to force 'Log Out of All Devices'.
Step 4: Run Full Diagnostic Scans — Execute a comprehensive anti-malware scan to remove persistent trojans or keyloggers.
Step 5: Monitor Financial Statements — Notify banking institutions immediately if unauthorized transactions appear.
cyber.content_UNDERSTANDINGMODERNS_3924:
UNDERSTANDING MODERN SOCIAL ENGINEERING VECTORS

• Email Phishing: Look for spoofed sender headers, urgent emotional triggers ('Immediate Account Suspension'), and hidden destination URLs.
• Smishing (SMS Scams): Unsolicited text messages claiming package delivery failures or bank KYC verification links.
• Quishing (QR Code Scams): Malicious QR codes placed over legitimate parking or payment displays that redirect to credential harvesting forms.
• Vishing & Deepfake Audio: Scammers using voice cloning technology over phone calls to impersonate colleagues or family members.
cyber.content_MODERNPASSWORDHYGIEN_1b20:
MODERN PASSWORD HYGIENE (NIST SPECIAL PUBLICATION 800-63B)

• Prioritize Length Over Complexity: A 16-character passphrase composed of memorable words is far stronger than an 8-character complex string.
• Adopt Password Managers: Zero-knowledge encrypted vaults eliminate human memory limitations and generate unique high-entropy secrets.
• Transition to Passkeys: Public-key cryptography (FIDO2/WebAuthn) replaces vulnerable passwords with hardware-backed biometric verification.
cyber.content_NETWORKDEVICEHARDENI_6f53:
NETWORK & DEVICE HARDENING GUIDELINES

• Public Wi-Fi Precautions: Never perform sensitive banking or corporate logins over unencrypted open Wi-Fi without a verified Virtual Private Network (VPN).
• Bluetooth & AirDrop Hardening: Disable discoverability when in public terminals or crowded transport hubs.
• IoT Network Isolation: Place smart TVs, cameras, and IoT home appliances on a dedicated Guest Wi-Fi network separated from primary work computers.

whatIsAi.title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
whatIsAi.p1: Imagine a computer that can learn to play chess, recognize your pet’s face, or even write a funny poem, without a human coding the rules step-by-step. That is Artificial Intelligence (AI)!
whatIsAi.p2: Normally, computers act like calculators—they only do exactly what we tell them to do using pre-written instructions. But AI acts more like a curious student. It learns by studying thousands of examples (called Data), finding patterns on its own, and getting smarter over time!
whatIsAi.p3: Just like how you learn to identify a mango by seeing it, smelling it, and tasting it a few times, an AI learns to identify a cat, a song, or a word by training on millions of pictures, audio clips, or sentences.
whatIsAi.funFact: The term "Artificial Intelligence" was actually invented way back in 1956 by a scientist named John McCarthy during a summer conference!

### Solving 3x - 7 = 14 Step-by-Step
- **Goal**: Find the value of variable 'x'.
- **Step 1 (Add 7 to both sides)**: To isolate the term with x, add 7 to both sides of the equation.
  - 3x - 7 + 7 = 14 + 7
  - 3x = 21
- **Step 2 (Divide both sides by 3)**: To find x, divide both sides by 3.
  - 3x / 3 = 21 / 3
  - x = 7
- **Verification**: Substitute x = 7 back into the original equation:
  - 3(7) - 7 = 21 - 7 = 14. This is correct!

### The Pythagorean Theorem

- **Simple Definition**: If you have a triangle with one 90-degree angle, multiplying the two shorter sides by themselves and adding them together will always equal the longest side multiplied by itself (a2 + b2 = c2).
- **Real-World Example**: Imagine a ladder leaning against a wall. The wall and the ground make a 90-degree angle. If you know the height of the wall and distance on the ground, Pythagoras tells you exactly how long the ladder is!
- **Proof Example**:
  - Side a = 3, Side b = 4
  - 3 squared + 4 squared = 9 + 16 = 25
  - Since c squared = 25, Side c (the longest side) must be 5!

ai.lessonLearnSub_1: Learn the secret 3-step formula to talk to AI!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_1:
Talking to AI is like giving instructions to a super-smart robot. If you just say 'help me', it gets confused! Use this systematic magic formula:

**1. Role**: Who should the AI pretend to be? (Example: 'Act as a funny science teacher')
**2. Task**: What do you want it to do? (Example: 'Explain gravity')
**3. Details**: What are the rules? (Example: 'Use a maximum of 3 sentences')

**Important Rules:**
- Be the Boss: Give clear and direct orders.
- Add Rules: Tell it exactly how long or short the answer should be.
- Give Examples: Show the AI exactly what you want the output to look like.
ai.lessonLearnSub_2: Ask the AI to explain the logic instead of just giving the answer!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_2:
If you ask an AI 'what is 2x + 5 = 15?', it will just say 'x = 5'. This doesn't help you learn! Instead, ask it to become a tutor.

**Systematic Example:**
**[Bad Prompt]**: 'Solve 2x + 5 = 15'
**[Super Prompt]**: 'Act as a patient math teacher. Solve 2x + 5 = 15 step-by-step. Explain the rule for each step, and verify the final answer at the end.'

**Important Rules:**
- Ask for Steps: Always include 'Solve this step-by-step'.
- Ask for the Rules: Tell it to explain the 'why' behind the math.
- Verify: Ask it to verify the answer by plugging it back into the equation.
ai.lessonLearnSub_3: Learn the exact layout for writing a professional school notice!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_3:
Notices are highly **FORMAL**. You must never use casual words like 'Hey' or 'Cool'. A school notice must follow a strict box format.

**Systematic Layout Rules:**
1. **School Name**: Top center.
2. **The Word 'NOTICE'**: Right below it, in capital letters.
3. **Date & Heading**: When and What.
4. **Body**: Very short (under 50 words).
5. **Sign-off**: Your name and designation (e.g., 'Head Boy').

**Example Prompt**: 'Act as a Head Girl. Write a formal 50-word school notice about a lost watch following the standard CBSE box format.'

**Important Rules:**
- Specify the Tone: Always ask for a 'highly formal and respectful tone'.
- Enforce the Layout: Command the AI to include the 'Date, Heading, and Signature'.
- Keep it Strict: Set a hard limit of 'maximum 50 words'.
ai.lessonLearnSub_4: How to tell AI to write casual, friendly, and exciting letters!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_4:
Unlike notices, **INFORMAL** letters and emails (to friends or family) are fun, relaxed, and full of emotion! You don't need a strict box format, but you do need the right vibe.

**Systematic Rules for Informal Prompts:**
1. **Greeting**: Use words like 'Dear Rohan' or 'Hi Uncle!'.
2. **Tone**: Tell the AI to use a 'warm, enthusiastic, and friendly tone'.
3. **Content**: It can be longer, chatty, and include personal feelings or jokes!

**Example Prompt**: 'Act as my funny best friend. Write an informal email inviting me to a weekend movie marathon. Use a very excited tone!'

**Important Rules:**
- Set the Emotion: Use words like 'excited', 'nostalgic', or 'funny' in your prompt.
- Casual Sign-off: Ask it to end with 'Lots of love' or 'Catch you later!'.
ai.lessonLearnSub_5: Tell the AI exactly how to organize your paragraphs!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_5:
A bad prompt like 'write an essay about lions' gives you a giant, boring wall of text that puts everyone to sleep.

To write an amazing essay, be an architect! Tell the AI exactly how to build it:

**Systematic Blueprint:**
1. **Title**: 'Start with a catchy headline.'
2. **Structure**: 'Write exactly 3 paragraphs.'
3. **Content Map**: 'Paragraph 1 is the Introduction. Paragraph 2 is about Family Life. Paragraph 3 is the Conclusion.'

This guarantees a beautifully structured essay every single time!

**Important Rules:**
- Tell the AI the layout: Demand subheadings for each section.
- Set a length limit: Give a strict limit like '100 words per paragraph'.
- Define the audience: 'Write this so a 10-year-old can understand it.'
ai.lessonLearnSub_6: Ask the AI to break down difficult text and create practice quizzes!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_6:
Ever read a paragraph in English class and thought, 'What does this even mean?!' AI can be your personal translator!

Instead of just asking 'explain this', use a **Systematic Learning Prompt**:

1. **Summarize**: 'Extract the 3 most important facts from this story.'
2. **Vocabulary**: 'Find 2 difficult words in the text and explain their meaning using simple examples.'
3. **Test Me**: 'Generate a multiple-choice question to test if I understood it.'

**Important Rules:**
- Ask for Bullet Points: It makes summaries much easier to read.
- Demand Simplicity: Tell the AI to 'explain it like I am 12 years old'.
- Self-Test: The best way to learn is by taking a mini-quiz at the end!
ai.lessonLearnSub_7: Learn complex science by comparing it to everyday fun things!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_7:
Science can have hard, scary words like 'chlorophyll' or 'stomata'. A boring prompt gives a boring textbook definition.

To make science fun, use **Metaphors** (comparisons)! Ask the AI to compare a confusing science topic to something you already understand.

**Systematic Example:**
**[Bad]**: 'Explain photosynthesis.'
**[Super]**: 'Explain photosynthesis by comparing the plant to a Chef cooking in a kitchen. Explain what the ingredients (sun, water, CO2) are, and what the final dish is!'

**Important Rules:**
- Use Metaphors: Compare atoms to LEGOs, or blood cells to delivery trucks.
- Simple Words: Ask the AI to explain terms in language a 6th grader can understand.
- Visuals: Ask it to describe what a diagram of the process would look like.
ai.lessonLearnSub_8: Turn boring science stages into an epic adventure story!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_8:
The water cycle has four major parts: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, and Collection. Memorizing them is boring!

Instead, ask the AI to write an **Adventure Story**.

**Systematic Trick:**
When you read a story about a little water droplet named 'Dewey' going on a wild skydive, your brain remembers the facts 10x better! Combine facts with fiction to create the perfect study notes.

**Important Rules:**
- Story Method: Ask the AI to explain a cycle by telling a story about a fun character.
- Force Vocabulary: Command the AI: 'You MUST include these exact scientific words...'
- Summary: Ask for a quick 1-sentence recap at the very end.
ai.lessonLearnSub_9: Describe colors, style, and lighting to generate masterpieces!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_9:
When using AI image generators, a simple prompt like 'a turtle' will give you a plain, boring photograph.

To make a masterpiece, you must act like a Hollywood Art Director! Build your prompt systematically:

1. **The Subject**: What is the main thing? (A turtle flying in space)
2. **The Medium/Style**: How is it drawn? (3D Pixar animation, or glowing neon chalk?)
3. **The Lighting**: Where is the light coming from? (Cinematic lighting, warm sunset, glowing edges)

**Important Rules:**
- Specify the Art Style: Use terms like '8-bit pixel art', 'watercolor', or 'cyberpunk'.
- Describe the Lighting: Lighting changes everything! Try 'golden hour' or 'neon glow'.
- Add fine details: Describe the character's clothing, expressions, and surroundings.
ai.lessonLearnSub_10: Prompt AI to write a thrilling story with characters and plot twists!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_10:
Writing a story is like directing a movie. If you just say 'write a story about a dog', the AI will write something very boring.

**Systematic Blueprint:**
1. **Setting**: Where does it happen? (e.g., A haunted forest in 2050).
2. **Characters**: Who is the hero? (e.g., Max, a robot dog).
3. **Conflict**: What is the problem? (e.g., He lost his battery).
4. **Resolution**: How does it end? (e.g., He uses solar power to save the day).

**Important Rules:**
- Set the Tone: Tell the AI if it should be scary, funny, or mysterious.
- Add Dialogue: Command the AI to include conversations between characters.
ai.lessonLearnSub_11: Command AI to rhyme and use rhythm perfectly!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_11:
Poems need rhythm, rhyming words, and deep meanings. A plain prompt gives a plain poem.

**Systematic Blueprint:**
1. **Topic & Theme**: What is the poem about? (e.g., A rainy day and feeling cozy).
2. **Structure**: How many stanzas (paragraphs)? (e.g., 3 stanzas).
3. **Rhyme Scheme**: AABB (every two lines rhyme) or ABAB (alternate lines rhyme).

**Important Rules:**
- Specify the Rhyme: Always tell the AI the exact rhyme scheme you want.
- Metaphors: Ask the AI to compare things (e.g., 'compare the rain to a dancer').
ai.lessonLearnSub_12: Learn to build strong arguments and counter-arguments!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_12:
In an argumentative essay, you must pick a side and defend it with logic. If you just ask AI to 'write about homework', it will just ramble.

**Systematic Blueprint:**
1. **Stance**: Tell the AI exactly which side to take (e.g., 'Homework should be banned').
2. **Arguments**: Ask for 3 strong logical points.
3. **Counter-Argument**: Acknowledge the other side (e.g., 'Some say homework helps practice, BUT...').
4. **Conclusion**: End with a powerful closing statement.

**Important Rules:**
- Use Transition Words: Tell AI to use words like 'Firstly', 'However', and 'In conclusion'.
- Stay Formal: Arguments should sound logical, not emotional.
ai.lessonLearnSub_13: Use the 5 senses to describe a scene vividly!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_13:
Descriptive writing is all about making the reader feel like they are inside the story. 

**Systematic Blueprint:**
Instead of saying 'The market was crowded', you must use **Sensory Details**:
1. **Sight**: What do you see? (Bright red apples, flashing neon signs).
2. **Sound**: What do you hear? (Honking horns, shouting vendors).
3. **Smell**: What do you smell? (Freshly baked bread, exhaust fumes).

**Important Rules:**
- Force Sensory Details: Explicitly command the AI: 'Describe what I can hear, see, and smell.'
- Use Adjectives: Ask it to use strong, descriptive adjectives.
ai.lessonLearnSub_14: Learn to describe an image and build a story around it!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_14:
In picture composition, you are given an image and asked to write a story about it. Since AI can't always 'see' your exam paper, you must become its eyes!

**Systematic Blueprint:**
1. **Describe the Image**: Tell the AI exactly what is in the picture. (e.g., 'A boy holding a broken kite under a tree').
2. **Background**: Ask the AI to guess what happened before the picture.
3. **Future**: Ask the AI to guess what happens after the picture.

**Important Rules:**
- Be highly detailed when describing the picture to the AI.
- Ask for a 'beginning, middle, and end' to make it a complete story.
ai.lessonLearnSub_15: Break down confusing word problems into simple facts!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_15:
Word problems in math can be tricky because there is too much text. AI can help you decode them!

**Systematic Blueprint:**
Instead of just asking for the answer, command the AI to dissect the problem:
1. **Given Facts**: What numbers do we already know?
2. **The Goal**: What exactly do we need to find?
3. **The Formula**: Which formula should we use?
4. **Step-by-Step Solution**: Show the working.

**Important Rules:**
- Never just ask for the answer. Ask for the 'Given Facts' and 'Formula' first!
ai.lessonLearnSub_16: Use AI to understand confusing theorems and shapes!
ai.lessonLearnDesc_16:
Geometry proofs can be very confusing. AI can explain them using simple logic and real-world examples.

**Systematic Blueprint:**
When struggling with a theorem (like Pythagoras or Properties of Triangles):
1. **Simple Definition**: Ask the AI to explain the theorem in one simple sentence.
2. **Real World Example**: Ask how this is used in real life (like building a house).
3. **Step-by-Step Proof**: Ask it to prove a simple example.

**Important Rules:**
- Always ask for a real-world application so your brain remembers it better!

lifeskills.heroDesc: Practical lessons and daily habits for an independent life.
lifeskills.card1_desc: Learn how to make simple, healthy and delicious meals for you and your family.
lifeskills.card1_content: Start with simple recipes like boiling eggs, making rice, and preparing a healthy salad. Always wash vegetables before cutting them and never leave a hot stove unattended!
lifeskills.card2_desc: Learn how to save money, budget your expenses, and make smart financial decisions.
lifeskills.card2_content: Budgeting helps you track what you earn and what you spend. Always save a portion of your allowance or income for the future. Wants vs Needs is the core of budgeting.
lifeskills.card3_desc: Master the safety checklist when withdrawing cash from an ATM machine securely.
lifeskills.card3_content: Always inspect the card reader slot for skimming devices by wiggling it. Shield the numeric keypad with your free hand while entering your secret PIN. Make sure the ATM screen fully resets before leaving the counter.
lifeskills.card4_desc: Learn crossing rules, traffic signals, and how to stay safe as a pedestrian on roads.
lifeskills.card4_content: Red light means Stop immediately. Yellow light means Get Ready. Green light means Go. Always cross at designated Zebra crossings, and look Left, Right, then Left again before stepping on the road.
lifeskills.card5_desc: Basic first aid skills everyone should know for emergencies.
lifeskills.card5_content: Clean a wound with soap and water, apply an antibacterial ointment, and cover it with a bandage. For minor burns, run cool water over it for 10 minutes.
lifeskills.card6_desc: Organize your day, set goals, and stop procrastinating.
lifeskills.card6_content: Create a daily schedule. Prioritize your most important tasks first (eat the frog!) and take short 5-minute breaks every 30 minutes to stay fresh.
lifeskills.card7_desc: Learn to express your thoughts clearly and listen to others.
lifeskills.card7_content: Good communication involves 50% speaking and 50% active listening. Maintain eye contact, don't interrupt, and ask questions to show you are engaged.
lifeskills.card8_desc: Fix simple things around the house without calling a professional.
lifeskills.card8_content: Learn to tighten a loose screw, change a lightbulb safely (always turn off the switch first!), and unclog a sink using a plunger or baking soda and vinegar.
lifeskills.card9_desc: Understand internet safety and basic computer hygiene.
lifeskills.card9_content: Never share your passwords with anyone. Always verify the source of emails before clicking any links, and keep your software updated.
lifeskills.card10_desc: Recognize and manage your own emotions and others.
lifeskills.card10_content: Pause and take a deep breath before reacting to anger. Try to understand things from the other person’s perspective before jumping to conclusions.
